sentences: (I) Cities are often several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside, a phenomenon known as the urban heat island effect.
(II) Many cities were originally founded beside rivers because transporting goods by water was cheaper than using roads.
(III) Concrete and asphalt absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night, keeping temperatures high long after sunset.
(IV) The lack of trees and open water removes the cooling effect that evaporation would otherwise provide.
(V) Planting trees and painting roofs white are among the simplest ways of reducing the effect.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf kentlerin neden daha sıcak olduğunu ([en:urban heat island]) ve çözümlerini anlatıyor; II. cümle şehirlerin neden nehir kıyısına kurulduğuna geçerek odağı bozuyor. I'den III'e geçiş doğal: önce etki tanımlanıyor, sonra nedenleri sayılıyor.

sentences: (I) The Romans built an extensive network of paved roads that connected the distant provinces to the capital.
(II) Roman concrete has survived for two thousand years, while modern concrete often cracks within a few decades.
(III) Researchers have recently discovered that the secret lies in small lumps of lime that were left in the mixture.
(IV) When water enters a crack, these lumps dissolve and form new crystals that seal the gap.
(V) Engineers are now trying to reproduce this self-healing property in modern building materials.
items.explain_tr: II–V cümleleri Roma betonunun neden dayanıklı olduğunu (kireç parçacıkları, kendini onarma) ve bugünkü uygulamalarını anlatıyor. I. cümle Roma yollarından söz ediyor; aynı dönem ama betonla ilgisi yok, paragrafın odağı dışında kalıyor.

sentences: (I) Procrastination is often blamed on laziness, but psychologists increasingly see it as a problem of emotion rather than of time management.
(II) People put off tasks that make them feel anxious, bored or inadequate, and the relief of avoiding the task is immediately rewarding.
(III) The reward, unfortunately, is short-lived, since the task remains and the anxiety usually grows.
(IV) Studies suggest that forgiving oneself for past delays reduces procrastination more effectively than self-criticism does.
(V) Time management courses are among the most popular training programmes offered by large companies.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf ertelemenin ([en:procrastination]) duygusal bir sorun olduğunu ve bununla nasıl başa çıkılacağını anlatıyor. V. cümle şirketlerin zaman yönetimi kurslarına geçiyor; ilk cümle bunun bir zaman yönetimi sorunu olmadığını söylediği için odak dağılıyor.

sentences: (I) Inflation measures how quickly the general level of prices rises over time.
(II) Central banks usually aim for a low, stable rate of around two per cent a year.
(III) When inflation rises above this target, they typically raise interest rates to discourage borrowing and spending.
(IV) Higher interest rates, however, also make it more expensive for businesses to invest, which can slow economic growth.
(V) The euro replaced the national currencies of twelve European countries in 2002.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf enflasyonu, merkez bankalarının hedefini ve faiz artışının etkilerini anlatıyor. V. cümle euronun kabul tarihine geçiyor; para konusu ama enflasyon ve faiz çizgisiyle bağ kurmuyor.

sentences: (I) Each year a tree adds a new ring of wood beneath its bark, and the width of the ring depends on the growing conditions.
(II) Oak is a popular choice for furniture because of its strength and its attractive grain.
(III) In a wet, warm year the ring is wide; in a year of drought it is narrow.
(IV) By matching patterns of wide and narrow rings, scientists can date wooden objects and reconstruct past climates.
(V) Using this method, researchers have traced a series of severe droughts that may explain the collapse of several ancient civilisations.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf ağaç halkalarıyla tarihleme ve geçmiş iklimi yeniden kurmayı anlatıyor; III'teki [en:the ring] I'deki halkaya gönderme yapıyor. II. cümle meşenin mobilyada kullanımına geçerek bu bağı koparıyor.

sentences: (I) Teenagers' body clocks shift during puberty, making it hard for them to fall asleep before eleven at night.
(II) Puberty also brings rapid physical growth and a marked increase in appetite.
(III) Yet most secondary schools begin lessons at eight or earlier, so many pupils arrive chronically short of sleep.
(IV) Schools that have moved their start time to nine o'clock report better attendance, fewer accidents and higher grades.
(V) Parents and employers, however, often object because later start times disrupt their own routines.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf ergenlerin uyku saatleri ile okulun başlama saatini tartışıyor. II. cümle ergenlikteki büyüme ve iştah değişimine geçiyor; I'deki [en:body clocks] ile III'teki [en:yet most secondary schools] doğrudan birbirine bağlı.

sentences: (I) Microplastics are fragments of plastic smaller than five millimetres, produced when larger items break down or shed fibres.
(II) They have now been found in the deepest ocean trenches, in Arctic snow and in the air above remote mountains.
(III) Plastic was first produced on an industrial scale in the early twentieth century and quickly replaced natural materials.
(IV) Marine animals swallow the particles, which then pass up the food chain and have been detected in human blood.
(V) The health effects of this exposure are still unknown, but scientists are urging that it be reduced as a precaution.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf mikroplastiklerin nerelerde bulunduğunu ve besin zincirindeki yolculuğunu anlatıyor. III. cümle plastiğin sanayi tarihine geçiyor; II'den IV'e ([en:the particles]) akış kesintisiz.

sentences: (I) When coffeehouses first appeared in London in the 1650s, they quickly became centres of business and political debate.
(II) For the price of a cup of coffee, a customer could read the newspapers, hear the latest news and argue with strangers for hours.
(III) Several famous institutions, including Lloyd's insurance market and the London Stock Exchange, began as coffeehouse gatherings.
(IV) Coffee beans are grown mainly in tropical regions, where the warm climate and rich soil suit the plant.
(V) The authorities grew so alarmed by the free discussion that the king briefly tried to close the coffeehouses in 1675.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf 17. yüzyıl Londra kahvehanelerinin toplumsal ve siyasi rolünü anlatıyor. IV. cümle kahvenin nerede yetiştiğine geçerek dönemi ve odağı değiştiriyor; III'ten V'e ([en:the authorities grew so alarmed by the free discussion]) geçiş doğal.

sentences: (I) Ride-hailing and food-delivery apps have created a new category of work in which people are paid per task rather than per hour.
(II) Supporters praise the flexibility this gives workers, who can choose when and how much to work.
(III) Food delivery has become especially popular among students, who often order late at night.
(IV) Critics respond that the flexibility is largely illusory, since workers must accept whatever jobs appear in order to earn a living.
(V) Courts in several countries have ruled that such workers are employees entitled to a minimum wage and paid holidays.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf platform işçiliğinde esneklik tartışmasını ve mahkeme kararlarını anlatıyor. III. cümle yemek siparişi veren öğrencilere, yani tüketicilere geçiyor; II'deki [en:flexibility] ile IV'teki [en:the flexibility is largely illusory] doğrudan bağlı.

sentences: (I) When a large enough proportion of a population is vaccinated, a disease can no longer spread easily, even among those who are not immune.
(II) This protection, known as herd immunity, is especially important for infants and for people whose immune systems are too weak for vaccination.
(III) The proportion required varies by disease: for measles, which is highly contagious, it is around ninety-five per cent.
(IV) When vaccination rates fall below this level, outbreaks return, as several European countries discovered in the last decade.
(V) The first vaccine was developed by Edward Jenner in 1796, using material taken from cowpox sores.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf toplumsal bağışıklığı ([en:herd immunity]) ve aşılama oranının önemini anlatıyor. V. cümle Jenner'in ilk aşısına, yani aşının tarihine geçiyor; IV ile biten akış zaten tamam.

sentences: (I) Several studies have found that students who take notes by hand remember lecture content better than those who type.
(II) Typing is fast enough to record a lecture almost word for word, so typists tend to transcribe rather than think.
(III) Writing by hand is slower, which forces students to select and rephrase the main points as they go.
(IV) Laptops have become lighter and cheaper over the past decade, and most universities now expect students to own one.
(V) It is this processing, rather than the pen itself, that appears to produce the advantage.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf el yazısıyla not almanın neden daha etkili olduğunu açıklıyor; V'teki [en:this processing] III'teki seçip yeniden ifade etme sürecine gönderme yapıyor. IV. cümle dizüstü bilgisayarların fiyatına geçerek bu bağı koparıyor.

sentences: (I) In the 1630s, the price of tulip bulbs in the Netherlands rose to extraordinary levels, with single bulbs reportedly selling for more than a house.
(II) Buyers were not gardeners but speculators, who hoped to sell the bulbs on at a higher price before they were ever planted.
(III) Tulips originally came to Europe from the Ottoman Empire, where they had been cultivated for centuries.
(IV) In February 1637 the market collapsed within days, leaving many people with contracts for bulbs that were suddenly worthless.
(V) Historians still disagree about how widespread the damage was, but the episode remains the classic example of a speculative bubble.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf 1630'lardaki lale balonunu, spekülatörleri ve çöküşü anlatıyor. III. cümle lalenin Avrupa'ya nereden geldiğine geçiyor; konu lale ama paragrafın spekülasyon çizgisiyle ilgisi yok.

sentences: (I) Noise is one of the most widespread forms of pollution in modern cities, yet it receives far less attention than air or water pollution.
(II) Long-term exposure to traffic noise has been linked to high blood pressure, heart disease and disturbed sleep.
(III) Children in schools near busy roads or airports also show slower progress in reading.
(IV) Some cities have responded by lowering speed limits, installing quieter road surfaces and restricting night flights.
(V) Many people enjoy listening to music at high volume, particularly at concerts and festivals.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf gürültü kirliliğinin sağlık etkilerini ve şehirlerin aldığı önlemleri anlatıyor. V. cümle insanların konserde yüksek sesle müzik dinlemeyi sevmesine geçiyor; bu, çevresel gürültü ve önlemler çizgisinin dışında kalıyor.

sentences: (I) Vegetarian diets have been followed for religious reasons in parts of Asia for thousands of years.
(II) Cultivated meat is produced by growing animal cells in a nutrient solution rather than by raising and slaughtering animals.
(III) Its supporters argue that it could sharply reduce the land, water and emissions associated with conventional livestock farming.
(IV) The first cultivated burger, unveiled in 2013, cost several hundred thousand dollars to produce.
(V) Since then costs have fallen dramatically, and a handful of countries have approved the product for sale.
items.explain_tr: II–V cümleleri yapay etin ([en:cultivated meat]) nasıl üretildiğini, avantajlarını ve maliyetinin düşüşünü anlatıyor. I. cümle Asya'daki dini vejetaryenliğe değiniyor; et yemeyle ilgili olsa da yapay et konusuna hiç girmiyor.

sentences: (I) The modern shipping container, introduced in the 1950s, is one of the least glamorous but most important inventions of the twentieth century.
(II) Before its arrival, cargo was loaded piece by piece by gangs of dockworkers, and a ship could spend more time in port than at sea.
(III) Containers can be moved from ship to train to lorry without being opened, which has cut handling costs by more than ninety per cent.
(IV) Modern cargo ships are so large that only a few ports in the world have docks deep enough to receive them.
(V) This fall in costs made it practical to manufacture goods on one side of the world and sell them on the other.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf standart konteynerin yükleme maliyetini nasıl düşürdüğünü anlatıyor; V'teki [en:this fall in costs] III'teki yüzde doksanlık düşüşe gönderme yapıyor. IV. cümle gemilerin büyüklüğüne geçerek bu bağı koparıyor.

sentences: (I) Throughout the twentieth century, average scores on intelligence tests rose by roughly three points per decade in almost every country where records were kept.
(II) Intelligence tests were first used on a large scale to select recruits for the American army in 1917.
(III) The trend, known as the Flynn effect, was so steady that tests had to be made harder every few years to keep the average at one hundred.
(IV) Explanations include better nutrition, smaller families, longer schooling and growing familiarity with abstract problem-solving.
(V) In several wealthy countries, however, the rise appears to have stopped or even reversed since the 1990s.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf zekâ testi puanlarındaki yükselişi ([en:Flynn effect]) ve nedenlerini anlatıyor; III'teki [en:the trend] I'deki yükselişe gönderme yapıyor. II. cümle testlerin 1917'de orduda kullanılmasına geçerek bu bağı koparıyor.

sentences: (I) As fresh water becomes scarcer, more countries are turning to desalination, the removal of salt from seawater.
(II) The most common method forces seawater through membranes fine enough to block salt molecules but not water.
(III) Sales of bottled water have grown rapidly in recent years, despite concerns about plastic waste.
(IV) The process is energy-intensive, and the concentrated brine left behind can harm marine life if it is discharged carelessly.
(V) Nevertheless, in dry coastal regions such as the Gulf states, desalination already supplies most of the drinking water.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf deniz suyunu tuzdan arındırmayı ([en:desalination]), yöntemini, bedelini ve kullanımını anlatıyor; IV'teki [en:the process] II'deki membran yöntemine gönderme yapıyor. III. cümle şişe su satışlarına geçerek bu bağı koparıyor.

sentences: (I) Predictions that the internet would make public libraries obsolete have so far proved wrong.
(II) Visits have fallen in some countries, but libraries have responded by redefining what they offer.
(III) Many now lend laptops and e-books, run coding clubs and language classes, and provide the only free internet access in poor neighbourhoods.
(IV) The Library of Alexandria, founded in the third century BC, was the largest collection of texts in the ancient world.
(V) For many users, the library has become less a store of books than a shared public space.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf kütüphanelerin dijital çağda nasıl dönüştüğünü anlatıyor. IV. cümle antik İskenderiye Kütüphanesi'ne geçiyor; kütüphane konusu ama zaman ve odak tamamen farklı. III'ten V'e ([en:for many users, the library has become…]) akış doğal.

sentences: (I) Large volcanic eruptions can cool the entire planet for a year or more.
(II) The eruption throws vast quantities of sulphur dioxide into the upper atmosphere, where it forms tiny droplets that reflect sunlight back into space.
(III) Volcanoes are found mainly along the boundaries of the tectonic plates, where the Earth's crust is weakest.
(IV) After the eruption of Mount Tambora in 1815, global temperatures fell by about half a degree, and 1816 became known in Europe as the year without a summer.
(V) Crops failed from Ireland to China, and food prices rose sharply.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf büyük volkan patlamalarının iklimi nasıl soğuttuğunu ve Tambora örneğini anlatıyor. III. cümle volkanların nerede bulunduğuna (levha sınırları) geçiyor; bu jeoloji bilgisi, iklim etkisi çizgisine uymuyor.

sentences: (I) In the 1840s, the Hungarian doctor Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that women whose babies were delivered by doctors died of fever far more often than those attended by midwives.
(II) He realised that the doctors often came directly from dissecting corpses and proposed that they carried something harmful on their hands.
(III) When he required them to wash their hands in a chlorine solution, the death rate fell dramatically.
(IV) Yet his colleagues rejected the idea, partly because it implied that they themselves were responsible for the deaths.
(V) Hospitals today employ specialist teams whose only task is to monitor and prevent infections.
items.explain_tr: Paragraf Semmelweis'ın 1840'lardaki el yıkama keşfini ve meslektaşlarının tepkisini anlatıyor. V. cümle bugünün hastanelerindeki enfeksiyon ekiplerine geçerek zamanı ve odağı değiştiriyor; I–IV tek bir tarihsel anlatı oluşturuyor.
